currentContext.business: KEC is a diversified global infrastructure EPC company that grew from origins in power transmission into six verticals - Power Transmission & Distribution, Civil, Transportation, Renewables, Oil & Gas Pipelines and Cables & Conductors - building grids, cities, pipelines, railway infrastructure and clean-energy systems. It delivers end-to-end T&D solutions (transmission lines, substations, HVDC, STATCOM), complex civil EPC projects (industrial facilities, high-rise buildings, water infrastructure, data centres and semiconductor manufacturing facilities), railway and urban transit EPC, solar/wind/BESS renewables and cross-country oil, gas and slurry pipelines, and through its wholly-owned subsidiary KEC Asian Cables Limited manufactures and supplies cables to over 95 countries. Its clients include Central and State Governments, Public Sector Undertakings, ministries, local municipal bodies and private sector customers.

Transportation: Metro Viaduct, Station, Power Supply & Traction

currentContext.strengths: Capabilities to execute projects in difficult terrains and conditions|Well-diversified across businesses and geographies, giving a resilient and de-risked model|Experienced professionals from 40 diverse nationalities|Digital and AI capabilities embedded across the project lifecycle|Well-integrated global supply chain|Unparalleled manufacturing, engineering and design capabilities|Backward integration of operations across Transmission & Distribution, Transportation and Renewables|Preferred contractor for ahead-of-schedule delivery of projects|Strong project management and execution capabilities|80+ years of operations and a global network of integrated manufacturing facilities and tower testing stations|End-to-end capabilities across the transmission value chain, executing over 110 projects across more than 30 countries
currentContext.strategies: Cables & Conductors: enter FY27 with a strategic agenda anchored on three pillars - portfolio advancement, network deepening and capability building.|Commercially launch E-beam and elastomeric cables to enter high-performance specialised segments (defence, automotive, railways), expanding the addressable market and reinforcing engineering credentials.|Continue scaling the cables dealer and distribution network, building on the momentum established in FY26.|Explore High Temperature Low Sag (HTLS) conductors and progress discussions with leading carbon core suppliers to serve next-generation transmission infrastructure domestically and internationally.|Run a structured digital transformation programme in the cables business, with digital and operational excellence initiatives continuing through FY27 to build internal infrastructure for data-driven execution at scale.|Civil: expand into high-value segments such as semiconductor, data centres and healthcare infrastructure while strengthening core buildings, water and public-infrastructure execution.|Civil: drive productivity via Project Xcelerate, undertaken in partnership with a leading global consulting firm, with deployment expanded across the business - state-of-the-art construction methods, digital tools and capability building at project sites.|Increase mechanised construction (automated plastering systems, prefabricated reinforcement solutions, advanced equipment) to reduce labour dependency and improve productivity.|Deploy digital tools - Building Information Modelling (BIM), AI-augmented project monitoring tools and dashboards, and material management platforms - to enhance planning accuracy, coordination and real-time execution visibility.|Transportation: strategically shift the portfolio towards technology-enabled segments such as signalling, safety systems and Kavach, while maintaining a disciplined, calibrated approach to bidding for conventional railway projects and limiting exposure to work on live railway tracks.|Transportation: participate in the growing ropeway market (supported by the Government's Parvatmala programme) with a calibrated approach to project selection and execution.|Close out legacy projects to streamline the project portfolio, improve capital efficiency and reduce exposure to execution-intensive contracts.|Oil & Gas Pipelines: expand the international footprint across the Middle East and Africa, building qualification credentials for larger-diameter pipeline, terminal and maintenance work.|Remain committed to delivering large-scale water supply schemes involving extensive pipeline networks and associated infrastructure despite delays in client funding allocation.|Dividend is recommended by the Board on the basis of the parameters set out in the Company's Dividend Distribution Policy and is placed before the Members for declaration at the Annual General Meeting; the Board recommended an equity dividend for the financial year ended March 31, 2026 on that basis. Non-Executive Chairman commission is paid within the overall limit of five percent of the net profit of the Company and requires Members' approval where it exceeds fifty percent of total annual remuneration payable to all Non-Executive Directors. On the entity side, capital is being reorganised within the group rather than deployed outward: the Board approved absorbing wholly owned subsidiary KEC Spur Infrastructure Private Limited into the Company and consolidating the Mauritius holding entity KEC Investment Holdings under KEC Towers LLC, both subject to approvals.|The Company engaged an external agency for its materiality assessment, identified 20 focus areas mapped against domestic and foreign peers and industry trends, and defined sustainability targets with respect to nine material issues based on ESG ratings assessed by reputed agencies.|BRSR Core indicators are subject to Reasonable Assurance by BSI Group India Private Limited; the BRSR reporting boundary was revised to a consolidated basis for FY 2025-26 (previous year was standalone).|EHS Policy in place with ISO 45001:2018 (occupational health and safety) implemented across all business verticals.|ISO 9001:2015 (quality management) implemented across all verticals.|Workforce diversity increased from 5% in FY22 to 8.3% in FY26; a Diversity committee and a separate D&I cell have been established, with steps including hiring transgenders, representation of female colleagues and an international workforce.|Employees are guided by the RPG Code of Corporate Governance & Ethics, and the internal control system includes a whistle-blower mechanism allowing directors, employees and third parties to report genuine concerns, misconduct or fraud without fear of retaliation, with direct access to the Chairman of the Audit Committee in exceptional cases.|Grievance redressal mechanisms are embedded in the respective policies substantiating the BRSR principles, published at https://www.kecrpg.com/policies; all pending employee, worker and customer complaints were closed after appropriate action during FY 2025-26.|Internal Audit operates a structured audit cycle ensuring every major area of the Company is reviewed at least once every three years, providing independent assurance on strategic, operational, financial, compliance and safety-related risks, with findings reported to the Audit Committee.|Local community development is treated as a material opportunity, with initiatives in education, employability, livelihood and health in the vicinity of operations; CSR is applicable under section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013.|Employee well-being and continuous learning are treated as durable priorities, with expansion of health, wellness and fitness initiatives and learning programmes across digital tools, analytics and emerging technologies.
currentContext.expansion: To support future growth, KEC continues to strengthen its manufacturing and execution capabilities. It operates a global network of integrated manufacturing facilities and tower testing stations and has undertaken capacity expansions over the years across its key locations, including Dubai, Jaipur, Jabalpur and Butibori (Nagpur), along with capacity augmentation in Brazil; these investments are expected to enhance production capacity, improve supply chain responsiveness and support execution across large-scale projects. Alongside physical capacity, the Company is building out capability in advanced, high-value segments - HVDC systems, STATCOMs and digital substations - to move up the value chain, and is enhancing project execution through increased mechanisation and adoption of advanced technologies such as crane-based tower erection, drone stringing, precast foundations and IoT-enabled monitoring systems, particularly for challenging terrains and large-scale transmission projects. The Company is currently executing a large and diversified portfolio of over 110 projects across more than 30 countries, and its first HVDC converter station project has been successfully commissioned in Maharashtra, with five HVDC projects currently under execution. Expansion of the addressable footprint is also being pursued commercially: the Civil business is entering new segments including Semiconductors, Hospitals, Thermal Power, Metals & Mining, Residential and Commercial real estate alongside core Buildings & Factories, Data Centres and Public Spaces, while SAE Towers in the Americas has grown its order book and L1 position and the Company continues to reduce debt levels there. No rupee capex outlay or capex schedule is disclosed in the routed text.
currentContext.mdna: India's cable and conductor market continues a structurally strong growth trajectory, driven by sustained public investment in power transmission and distribution, rapid scaling of renewable energy capacity, expanding 5G and fibre infrastructure, growing data centre ecosystems and accelerated railway modernisation.|Shift towards underground cabling in densely populated urban centres, increasing EV infrastructure deployment and defence indigenisation programmes are creating additional demand vectors for specialised and high-performance cable solutions.|Globally, the energy transition is reshaping procurement priorities, with buyers placing increasing weight on sustainability credentials, technical performance and supply chain resilience.|Growth in the cables dealer segment: order book from the dealer segment grew 57% in FY26, a direct outcome of deepened channel engagement and systematic scaling of the distribution footprint.|Civil: sustained government investment in water supply, urban mobility, airports and social infrastructure, plus increasing urbanisation and expansion of metro rail networks, are expected to support long-term demand.|Transportation outlook remains positive with increasing investments in railway safety systems, signalling and urban transit infrastructure; however, execution challenges and moderation in conventional railway infrastructure opportunities continue to impact the sector.|Kavach deployment is part of a broader national programme to enhance railway safety and modernise signalling; this segment involves higher system integration and offers relatively improved execution visibility versus conventional railway projects.|Ropeways are emerging as a new segment in India's transportation ecosystem, supported by the Government's Parvatmala programme and increasing private sector participation.|Oil & Gas: the Government of India's plan to expand the natural gas pipeline network to approximately 34,000 km (from approximately 25,500 km currently), along with expansion of refining capacity from 256 MMTPA to over 300 MMTPA, is expected to drive future investments in pipeline infrastructure.|Oil & Gas: international markets in the Middle East and Africa are expected to provide growth avenues, supported by strengthening qualification credentials and increasing participation in opportunities.|Near-term Oil & Gas headwind: subdued domestic pipeline tendering activity and significantly increased competition from smaller city-gas-distribution (CGD) contractors.|Railway sector execution remains constrained by right-of-way (RoW) issues, dependency on traffic blocks and coordination across multiple stakeholders; urban transit timelines remain influenced by land acquisition and multi-agency coordination.|Cables business order intake stood at around ` 2,500 Crore in FY26, registering 11% year-on-year growth, reflecting an improving competitive position across both domestic and international markets.|Order book from the cables dealer segment grew 57% during FY26.|Oil & Gas Pipelines order inflows improved to approximately ` 200 Crore during the year, compared to over ` 50 Crore in FY25, driven by the Company's first orders in the Middle East (a station works project in Saudi Arabia and a terminal station works project in Benin).|The Company received direct approval for onshore pipeline works in the Middle East and submitted qualifications for pipeline and terminal maintenance projects with leading oil and gas operators, expanding the addressable opportunity set across the Middle East and Africa.

risks.note: High dependence on a single geography may create concentration risk in growth, execution and recovery of receivables. The Company monitors geographic exposure - particularly in regions with heightened geopolitical uncertainty - through regular reviews of order book, order intake and project portfolio, places guardrails to limit overall exposure in a single geography and explores adequate insurance coverage.

Political instability, regional conflicts, trade restrictions and policy changes in certain markets may disrupt supply chains, impact project execution and delay collections. Mitigation includes assessing the viability of continuing operations in affected regions, alternative strategic sourcing and evaluating ECGC and other suitable risk covers. Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East during Q4 FY26 were an explicitly flagged feature of the operating environment.

Delays arising from right-of-way issues, land and forest clearances, challenging terrain, supply chain disruptions and labour availability may impact project execution, profitability and cash flows. Mitigation includes clear scope boundaries, tender contingency provisions, a shift toward mechanisation (crane-based tower erection, automated civil equipment) and a dynamic cost-compensation framework to re-negotiate project costs on unforeseen external delays.

Exposure to fluctuations in prices of key commodities such as steel, zinc, copper and aluminium may impact project profitability. Mitigated by maintaining optimal hedge levels with central monitoring and periodic management review; in certain projects materials are supplied by the customer, who also bears price escalation.

Given the scale, complexity and duration of EPC projects, contractual disputes, claims and litigation may arise, potentially impacting project outcomes and financial performance. Mitigated by a structured contract review and approval process supported by dedicated legal and commercial teams, with learnings from past disputes fed into future negotiations.

Labour shortages were experienced by the industry throughout the year and constrained Civil revenues alongside delayed release of work fronts. Permanent-worker turnover rose to 39% in FY 2025-26 from 12% in FY 2024-25 (permanent employee turnover 25%), a structural execution constraint for a labour-intensive EPC model; the workforce strategy includes enhanced remuneration, upgraded labour amenities and a deliberate shift toward mechanisation.

Identified in the BRSR materiality assessment as a risk: ensuring a safe workplace and continuity of operations across all verticals is critical to mitigating work-related injuries and illnesses and supporting uninterrupted project execution; safety incidents may reduce employee productivity and affect business deliverables. The Company has an EHS Policy and ISO 45001:2018 implemented across all business verticals.

risks.risk: Quality, service delivery and customer centricity
risks.note: Identified in the BRSR materiality assessment as a risk: losing customers' confidence may impact the flow of new orders and hamper business growth. Mitigated through ISO 9001:2015 implemented across all verticals and a customer complaint redressal process with restricted resolution timelines.

one-line thesis: KEC is leveraging a record Rs.30,000cr order book plus L1 to drive growth across civil, T&D, and railways, despite near-term margin pressure from Brazil losses and commodity inflation; margins are expected to rebound sharply from Q3FY23 as legacy contracts complete, commodity costs soften, and working capital improves.
financial scorecard: rev: +31% YoY; EBITDA: 5.1% consolidated (down from prior); PAT: 0.9% consolidated (down); orderbook: Rs.23,720cr; netdebt: Rs.3,418cr (up from prior)
guidance: 15-20% YoY order intake growth over next 2-3 years; targeting double-digit consolidated EBITDA margins by FY24; SAE Brazil losses to resolve by Q3FY23; working capital days to improve to ~130-135 by FY23 end.
order book & pipeline: Rs.23,720cr (as of Jun 30, 2022); L1 pipeline: Rs.8,000cr; total order book + L1: Rs.30,000cr (record); T&D: Rs.11,380cr in Americas; Civil: Rs.10,000cr+; Railways: Rs.6,500cr+; Oil & Gas: Rs.1,000cr+
segment / subsidiary detail: T&D: Rs.1,645cr revenue (+17% YoY); India & Americas strong; secured India's first 765kV digital substation; Brazil EPC projects nearly complete; Railways: Rs.700cr revenue (+19% YoY); double-digit EBITDA; L1 for Rs.1,000cr+ international orders; Civil: Rs.600cr revenue (+2x YoY); order intake Rs.1,200cr; order book + L1 >Rs.10,000cr; Oil & Gas: Rs.92cr revenue; secured Rs.105cr order; Cables: Rs.419cr revenue (+26% YoY); new railway product facility operational; backward integration enhancing rail segment
growth verticals / optionality: International expansion in Middle East (Abu Dhabi, Saudi, Bangladesh), Americas (Mexico plant fully loaded), and Brazil hardware orders; metro rail and Kavach signaling tech as high-growth niches; potential entry into data center infrastructure; green energy corridor tenders (GIB/TBCB) pending release
margins & cost dynamics: Consolidated EBITDA: 5.1% (impacted by Brazil losses, commodity inflation, logistics); Standalone EBITDA: 8.2%; T&D margins depressed by legacy fixed-price contracts and Brazil; Civil margins near double-digit; Railways double-digit EBITDA; commodity prices softening in H1FY23; freight costs up 3-4x in Africa/Middle East; interest cost consolidated: 3% (up from 2.6% standalone due to Brazil)
capex / expansion: Rs.700-800cr over last 3 years; new railway product manufacturing facility inaugurated; Mexico plant fully utilized; no major new capex announced; focus on mechanization/automation to improve productivity
capital allocation: Prioritizing debt reduction to normalized Rs.2,500cr level (ex-acceptances); funding Brazil losses and working capital; no dividend or buyback mentioned; equity infusion into SAE Brazil possible if profitability improves; working capital release expected from GST correction (Rs.250-300cr/year) and project completions
risks & watch-items: SAE Brazil debt (Rs.400cr) and interest cost (17-18%); delayed claims settlement (Rs.60-100cr); Afghanistan exposure (Rs.250cr stuck); prolonged working capital cycle (150 days); margin pressure from legacy T&D contracts; currency volatility in Brazil; regulatory delays in metro projects (e.g., DMRC green clearance); potential order conversion delays
management quality / tone: Confident and optimistic on long-term growth; acknowledges near-term headwinds but emphasizes resolution timeline (Q2-Q3); highlights record order book and pipeline as validation of strategy; proactive on cost controls, hedging, and GST reform benefits; committed to margin recovery and debt normalization
non-obvious takeaways: GST rate hike from 12% to 18% on EPC projects (July 18, 2022) will release Rs.500cr+ in accumulated tax credits over 2 years — a major hidden working capital tailwind; KEC's 'L1 pipeline' of Rs.8,000cr is a leading indicator of future order inflow, not just backlog; Brazil's shift from EPC to hardware supply post-project completion reduces execution risk and improves cash flow

themes.title: Power transmission & renewable-evacuation capex
themes.need: Grid build-out to evacuate ~90 GW of new renewables is the broadest theme in the universe - pulling EHV/765kV transmission EPC, towers, conductors, OPGW, cables and HVDC. POWERGRID/ADANIENSOL TBCB pipeline plus state RDSS/underground-cabling capex (Rajesh Power 544291, OMPOWER) underpins multi-year visibility for EPC, tower (KP Green 544150, SKIPPER) and conductor/cable makers (KEI, RRKABEL, DYCL).
themes.driver: Fresh TBCB awards + execution ramp; EPC order inflows over next 1-2 quarters.

hero.oneLiner: KEC International Limited, the flagship company of the RPG Group, is a global infrastructure Engineering, Procurement and Construction (EPC) major operating across six business verticals in more than 110 countries.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: KEC International Limited, the flagship company of the RPG Group, is a global infrastructure Engineering, Procurement and Construction (EPC) major operating across six business verticals in more than 110 countries.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: KEC is a diversified global infrastructure EPC company that grew from origins in power transmission into six verticals - Power Transmission & Distribution, Civil, Transportation, Renewables, Oil & Gas Pipelines and Cables & Conductors - building grids, cities, pipelines, railway infrastructure and clean-energy systems. It delivers end-to-end T&D solutions (transmission lines, substations, HVDC, STATCOM), complex civil EPC projects (industrial facilities, high-rise buildings, water infrastructure, data centres and semiconductor manufacturing facilities), railway and urban transit EPC, solar/wind/BESS renewables and cross-country oil, gas and slurry pipelines, and through its wholly-owned subsidiary KEC Asian Cables Limited manufactures and supplies cables to over 95 countries. Its clients include Central and State Governments, Public Sector Undertakings, ministries, local municipal bodies and private sector customers.

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: 15-20% YoY order intake growth over next 2-3 years; targeting double-digit consolidated EBITDA margins by FY24; SAE Brazil losses to resolve by Q3FY23; working capital days to improve to ~130-135 by FY23 end.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: International expansion in Middle East (Abu Dhabi, Saudi, Bangladesh), Americas (Mexico plant fully loaded), and Brazil hardware orders; metro rail and Kavach signaling tech as high-growth niches; potential entry into data center infrastructure; green energy corridor tenders (GIB/TBCB) pending release

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's cable and conductor market continues a structurally strong growth trajectory, driven by sustained public investment in power transmission and distribution, rapid scaling of renewable energy capacity, expanding 5G and fibre infrastructure, growing data centre ecosystems and accelerated railway modernisation.
- Shift towards underground cabling in densely populated urban centres, increasing EV infrastructure deployment and defence indigenisation programmes are creating additional demand vectors for specialised and high-performance cable solutions.
- Globally, the energy transition is reshaping procurement priorities, with buyers placing increasing weight on sustainability credentials, technical performance and supply chain resilience.
- Growth in the cables dealer segment: order book from the dealer segment grew 57% in FY26, a direct outcome of deepened channel engagement and systematic scaling of the distribution footprint.
- Civil: sustained government investment in water supply, urban mobility, airports and social infrastructure, plus increasing urbanisation and expansion of metro rail networks, are expected to support long-term demand.
- Transportation outlook remains positive with increasing investments in railway safety systems, signalling and urban transit infrastructure; however, execution challenges and moderation in conventional railway infrastructure opportunities continue to impact the sector.
- Kavach deployment is part of a broader national programme to enhance railway safety and modernise signalling; this segment involves higher system integration and offers relatively improved execution visibility versus conventional railway projects.
- Ropeways are emerging as a new segment in India's transportation ecosystem, supported by the Government's Parvatmala programme and increasing private sector participation.
- Oil & Gas: the Government of India's plan to expand the natural gas pipeline network to approximately 34,000 km (from approximately 25,500 km currently), along with expansion of refining capacity from 256 MMTPA to over 300 MMTPA, is expected to drive future investments in pipeline infrastructure.
- Oil & Gas: international markets in the Middle East and Africa are expected to provide growth avenues, supported by strengthening qualification credentials and increasing participation in opportunities.
- Near-term Oil & Gas headwind: subdued domestic pipeline tendering activity and significantly increased competition from smaller city-gas-distribution (CGD) contractors.
- Railway sector execution remains constrained by right-of-way (RoW) issues, dependency on traffic blocks and coordination across multiple stakeholders; urban transit timelines remain influenced by land acquisition and multi-agency coordination.
- Cables business order intake stood at around ` 2,500 Crore in FY26, registering 11% year-on-year growth, reflecting an improving competitive position across both domestic and international markets.
- Order book from the cables dealer segment grew 57% during FY26.
- Oil & Gas Pipelines order inflows improved to approximately ` 200 Crore during the year, compared to over ` 50 Crore in FY25, driven by the Company's first orders in the Middle East (a station works project in Saudi Arabia and a terminal station works project in Benin).
- The Company received direct approval for onshore pipeline works in the Middle East and submitted qualifications for pipeline and terminal maintenance projects with leading oil and gas operators, expanding the addressable opportunity set across the Middle East and Africa.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Consolidated EBITDA: 5.1% (impacted by Brazil losses, commodity inflation, logistics); Standalone EBITDA: 8.2%; T&D margins depressed by legacy fixed-price contracts and Brazil; Civil margins near double-digit; Railways double-digit EBITDA; commodity prices softening in H1FY23; freight costs up 3-4x in Africa/Middle East; interest cost consolidated: 3% (up from 2.6% standalone due to Brazil)

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Prioritizing debt reduction to normalized Rs.2,500cr level (ex-acceptances); funding Brazil losses and working capital; no dividend or buyback mentioned; equity infusion into SAE Brazil possible if profitability improves; working capital release expected from GST correction (Rs.250-300cr/year) and project completions

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: To support future growth, KEC continues to strengthen its manufacturing and execution capabilities. It operates a global network of integrated manufacturing facilities and tower testing stations and has undertaken capacity expansions over the years across its key locations, including Dubai, Jaipur, Jabalpur and Butibori (Nagpur), along with capacity augmentation in Brazil; these investments are expected to enhance production capacity, improve supply chain responsiveness and support execution across large-scale projects. Alongside physical capacity, the Company is building out capability in advanced, high-value segments - HVDC systems, STATCOMs and digital substations - to move up the value chain, and is enhancing project execution through increased mechanisation and adoption of advanced technologies such as crane-based tower erection, drone stringing, precast foundations and IoT-enabled monitoring systems, particularly for challenging terrains and large-scale transmission projects. The Company is currently executing a large and diversified portfolio of over 110 projects across more than 30 countries, and its first HVDC converter station project has been successfully commissioned in Maharashtra, with five HVDC projects currently under execution. Expansion of the addressable footprint is also being pursued commercially: the Civil business is entering new segments including Semiconductors, Hospitals, Thermal Power, Metals & Mining, Residential and Commercial real estate alongside core Buildings & Factories, Data Centres and Public Spaces, while SAE Towers in the Americas has grown its order book and L1 position and the Company continues to reduce debt levels there. No rupee capex outlay or capex schedule is disclosed in the routed text.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident and optimistic on long-term growth; acknowledges near-term headwinds but emphasizes resolution timeline (Q2-Q3); highlights record order book and pipeline as validation of strategy; proactive on cost controls, hedging, and GST reform benefits; committed to margin recovery and debt normalization

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: SAE Brazil debt (Rs.400cr) and interest cost (17-18%); delayed claims settlement (Rs.60-100cr); Afghanistan exposure (Rs.250cr stuck); prolonged working capital cycle (150 days); margin pressure from legacy T&D contracts; currency volatility in Brazil; regulatory delays in metro projects (e.g., DMRC green clearance); potential order conversion delays

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: GST rate hike from 12% to 18% on EPC projects (July 18, 2022) will release Rs.500cr+ in accumulated tax credits over 2 years — a major hidden working capital tailwind; KEC's 'L1 pipeline' of Rs.8,000cr is a leading indicator of future order inflow, not just backlog; Brazil's shift from EPC to hardware supply post-project completion reduces execution risk and improves cash flow

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Merger] "Initiated the merger of our wholly owned subsidiary, KEC Spur Infrastructure Private Limited, with KEC International Limited"; the Oil & Gas Pipelines portfolio "will be integrated into our Civil - Hydrocarbon segment, enabling a unified approach towards hydrocarbon projects".
- [Geopolitics] Middle East / West Asia geopolitical uncertainty is listed as a headwind causing "Supply chain and logistics disruptions", "Elevated costs and longer lead times globally", "Revenue and margin timing impact" and "Delays in finalisation and award of projects in the Middle East".
- [Claims/receivables] Headwinds include "Delay in legal closure of disputes/ settlement of claims in Transportation and Metro projects", "Delay in payments in Water projects leading to slower progress and impacting working capital", and "Continued ROW issues in India T&D".
- [Leadership] Vimal Kejriwal is Managing Director & CEO and H. V. Goenka is Chairman (Non Executive Director); the board is listed with seven Non Executive Independent Directors.
- [Structure] SAE Towers is run as a distinct T&D unit (CEO - SAE Towers & ED - T&D (Africa & CIS)) and is reported separately within the T&D revenue split; KEC Asian Cables Ltd. has its own Managing Director.
